entities.summary:
The Battle of Mohi, fought on April 11, 1241, was a pivotal clash between Hungarian forces and the Mongol Empire's Golden Horde. 

As the Mongols swept into Eastern Europe, the Hungarians, led by King Béla IV, attempted to hold back the invaders at the town of Mohi. The battle was a decisive Mongol victory, marking the beginning of the end of Hungarian independence.

The consequences of the Battle of Mohi were far-reaching. The Mongols went on to conquer much of Eastern Europe, including modern-day Hungary, Poland, and Ukraine. The battle marked the end of the Golden Age of Hungary and had a lasting impact on the region's politics, culture, and demographics.

In the aftermath of the battle, the Mongols left a trail of destruction and chaos in their wake. The once-thriving towns and cities of Hungary were reduced to rubble, and the population was decimated. The battle also marked the beginning of the end of the Kingdom of Hungary, paving the way for the rise of the Ottoman Empire.

The 1241 Battle of Mohi stands as a testament to the Mongols' military prowess and their ability to adapt to different environments and cultures. As one historian noted, 'The Mongols were a force of nature, unstoppable and unrelenting in their pursuit of conquest.'
